entity.description:
GreptimeDB is the open-source Observability 2.0 database — treating metrics, logs, and traces as unified wide events instead of three separate pillars.

The three-pillar model (Prometheus + Loki + Jaeger) creates data silos, redundant infrastructure, and cross-system correlation pain. GreptimeDB replaces all three with one columnar engine on object storage, enabling cross-signal SQL JOINs, up to 50x cost reduction, and native support for emerging workloads like AI agent observability.

Why teams switch:
▪️Logs: Full-text indexing where Loki only indexes labels. 10x faster queries, 30% lower TCO. (OB Cloud: billions of logs daily across 170+ availability zones.)
▪️Metrics: Compute-storage separation — no more Thanos/Mimir complexity. SQL + PromQL replaces Prometheus + your data warehouse.
▪️Traces: Columnar storage vs. ES inverted indexes — 45x less storage, Jaeger-compatible, one-week migration.
▪️AI/LLM: Store high-volume conversation data, agent traces, and token metrics via OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions.

Written in Rust, OpenTelemetry-native, deploys on Kubernetes with compute-storage separation. Used in production by teams processing billions of data points daily.

entity.name: Manifest
entity.description:
Coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot have shown how much developer velocity AI can unlock, but the code they write only works if it fits the environment it deploys into. Until now, this context has lived in the heads of senior engineers, architects, and platform teams. A developer who needs it pings someone, digs through Slack, or learns it the hard way after an outage. That works, slowly. Agents don't have that option at all. Connection pool limits, IAM scopes, mesh policies, secret bindings, downstream consumers, live drift—none of it is in the code, and none of it is in any place an agent can reach.

We've built Manifest to compile that context into software. We continuously assemble a deterministic, time-versioned graph of the customer's full application stack: code, IaC, cloud, Kubernetes, IAM, secrets, mesh, CI/CD, on-prem. The architectural commitment is retrieval separated from reasoning. The graph is built once, continuously, and queryable as data, so the agents reasoning on top don't each have to investigate the environment from scratch. The graph is the context layer that developers and coding agents query before they make a change, so the code (whether written by a human or an agent) fits the system it's about to touch. Because the graph captures every change attributed to actor and timestamp, configuration drift and unauthorized changes surface the moment they happen instead of being discovered weeks later in an outage or audit.

Manifest works from the earliest moments of the lifecycle. Developers and agents query the graph in dev to understand blast radius before code is written. CI pipelines query it to validate changes before merge. Staging queries it to catch drift between IaC and actual state. By the time a change reaches production, it's already been validated at every step. One graph, every agent.

candidates.rationale: Manifest provides infrastructure context and pre-deployment change validation for coding agents, not production observability, APM, logging, or security monitoring.
